units.description: imports resolve across the whole hcli package
full unit suite, gated on imports resolving first

rungs.rejected_as_equilibrium: only 1.3% over c=4, below the 5.0% bar

equilibrium_rule: the highest rung that beat its predecessor by more than 5% in VERIFIED units per hour -- the knee, not the argmax, and explicitly not the largest integer reached
critical_path_bound: completion p95 is flat at ~84.9s across every rung because one unit (the full unit suite) dominates it, and total wall converges to ~128s at c=4 and c=8 alike. Past c=4 this campaign is CRITICAL-PATH bound, not capacity bound: adding workers cannot beat the longest chain.

scope_honesty.what_this_measured: CPU/TEST-class concurrency, end to end, through HCLI's own scheduler, over 23 real WorkUnits whose acceptance is each command's own exit code.
scope_honesty.what_this_did_NOT_measure: It is NOT a MIXED campaign. Every unit ran on the CPU backend; the engine was a NullEngine that refuses to execute a unit, so no Qwen cognition and no Grok dispatch took part. It therefore does NOT satisfy HCLI_MIXED_MAX (G019) or HCLI_GROK_MAX_EQUILIBRIUM (G015), both of which require the other backends to be in the run.
scope_honesty.what_it_DOES_satisfy: MAX_NO_ARTIFICIAL_WORK (G018), and it supplies a measured useful equilibrium for the CPU class.

earlier_attempt_and_why_it_was_wrong.symptom: the first run reported peak_actually_active=22 at rungs 1, 2 AND 4, with flat throughput of 329.7 / 314.7 / 314.8 WU/h
earlier_attempt_and_why_it_was_wrong.cause: the rung was decoration. runtime_count gates GPU_DECODE, while the TEST class is capped at ncpu, so every ready unit ran at once whatever the rung said and the independent variable never varied.
earlier_attempt_and_why_it_was_wrong.fix: the rung now sets ResourceLimits.test directly. peak_actually_active is now 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, matching the request.
also_repaired: chain.suite exceeded the executor's 120s CPU timeout and failed for a reason unrelated to what it checks, then retried into the same wall; the campaign now sets HCLI_CPU_TIMEOUT=600
prop.p0gates exits 1 when P0-7 is INCONCLUSIVE, which depends on whether a Grok lane happens to be live; the unit now asks only for the environment-independent gates

equilibrium_rule_correction.was: argmax of verified units per hour, which selected c=8
equilibrium_rule_correction.why_wrong: c=8 beat c=4 by 1.27% for twice the concurrency. Selecting it is exactly the 'largest integer reached' the directive warns against.
equilibrium_rule_correction.now: the highest rung beating its predecessor by more than 5%, which selects c=4

finding_critical_path_bound: completion p95 is flat at ~84.9s at every rung, because one unit -- the full unit suite -- dominates it, and total wall converges to 129.6s at c=4 and 128.0s at c=8. Past c=4 this campaign is CRITICAL-PATH bound, not capacity bound: more workers cannot beat the longest chain. That is also why queue delay collapses from 67.1s at c=1 to 0.16s at c=8 while throughput does not follow -- the queue empties, the chain does not shorten.
coincidence_noted_not_claimed: The CPU-class equilibrium (4) equals the measured Qwen decode equilibrium (4). Different workloads on the same machine; this is most likely the box's parallelism showing through twice, not a shared law. Recorded as an observation, not a conclusion.
